h: Getting ready for a day on the high seas
p: A bit of preparation helps everyone get the most from the waterpark. Pack swimwear, a towel each, flip-flops for walking around and a change of warm clothes for the trip home. Goggles are a good shout for anyone who doesn't like water in their eyes, especially near the tipping bucket, and a water bottle keeps everyone going. Lockers make life easier, so you're not worrying about bags and valuables while you're in the water.

Check the ride rules together before you go so everyone knows what they can try. Younger children often start in the Sunken Galleon and build up the courage for the flumes. Older kids and adults will want to head straight for the Terror Torrent, but it's worth warming up first.
How long to allow? Your session will set the pace, but plan to arrive early enough to get changed without rushing. Little ones will need breaks, so build in time for snacks and warming up.

Barnsley has plenty to round off a family day. Cannon Hall Farm, in the countryside near Cawthorne, is a big favourite with families, with animals to meet, play areas and a farm shop, and the house and parkland at Cannon Hall next door are lovely for a walk. Wentworth Castle Gardens has historic gardens and a striking hilltop folly. For a bit of history, Elsecar Heritage Centre brings together old industrial buildings, independent shops and a heritage railway.

In town, Locke Park is a nice place to stretch your legs, with its tall tower and big views. The Glass Works and Barnsley's market are also worth a wander if you fancy a bit of shopping before heading home.
